proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG / SPECIAL REVENUE FUNDS / FISCAL YEAR ENDING 6/30/13`, PDF pages 71-75 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed pages 67-71). Five pages, ONE table. NO PAGE HAS A TEXT LAYER; each was read off its own 400 dpi bitmap. COLUMN NAMES READ OFF THE PRINTED HEADER (rule 13b.4), verbatim and with the page's own dates: `PROGRAM NAME` | `FORWARD 7/1/2012` | `TOTAL RECEIPTS` | `TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS` | `BALANCE FWD 7/1/2013`. The header is reprinted at the top of all five pages. Figures in parentheses are stored NEGATIVE, as the page prints them -- including the FEMA grant's DISBURSEMENTS of ($3,209.47), a negative disbursement. A blank cell is NOT a zero and is left empty. Each row also carries the section heading the page prints above it (GENERAL GOVERNMENT, SCHOOL DEPARTMENT, PUBLIC SAFETY, PARKS & RECREATION, HIGHWAY DEPT., COUNCIL ON AGING, LIBRARY, CEMETERIES, UNCLASSIFIED); the page prints NO subtotal for any section. THE CHECK: 126 funds, and ALL FOUR COLUMNS sum to the `GRAND TOTAL` the table prints on its last page, to the cent -- 2,062,621.79 / 5,844,092.35 / 5,697,713.47 / 2,209,000.67. No tolerance is declared and none was needed. AND A SECOND CHECK THAT IS STATED HERE RATHER THAN ASSERTED BY THE VERIFIER. Every row states an identity -- forward plus receipts less disbursements is the balance carried forward -- and ALL 126 ROWS CLOSE TO THE CENT, verified in the same pass that produced this file. It is not DECLARED as a `row_identity` because `verify_page_reads.py` expresses an identity as `a,b,c=d` (all added) or `a-b-c=d` (first added, rest subtracted), and this one has TWO added terms and one subtracted. Negating the disbursements column to fit the grammar would mean storing a sign the document does not print, and declaring a wrong form and attesting the rows that then fail would be attesting our own limitation as the town's error. So the published check is the one the document itself states: the four printed column totals. WHY THIS TABLE MATTERS (CLAUDE.md rule 11). These are the funds that pay for real staff and real programmes and appear NOWHERE in the general fund appropriations schedule: School Lunch, School Choice, Non-Resident Tuition, the Extended Day revolving fund, Chapter 90 highway money, Title I, PL 94-142, the 50/50 Sped tuition grant and the rest. A general-fund line that rises because one of these ended looks identical, in the budget, to a line that rises because the town bought more. This page is the only place the FY2013 report says what any of them held. WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW: a fund balance is not a programme's cost and not a headcount. The table gives receipts and disbursements by FUND and never says what was bought or who was paid.
